# The doodle panel library

61 hand-drawn vertical panels (1080×1935) shipped in
`public/doodles`, catalogued in `src/lib/visuals/doodles.ts`. They are the
house style for AI-visual mode: a creator who picks **AI images** gets a panel
from here whenever one honestly fits the teaching, and Grok only draws when
nothing does.

**Why reuse first.** A shipped panel is instant, costs nothing, and — unlike a
generation — is a frame someone has already looked at and approved. Reuse is
not the cheap path here, it is the reliable one.

## How a panel gets picked

`matchDoodle()` scores every panel against the teaching:

- a hit on the model's own `visualTerms` scores **3**
- a hit on a noun merely present in the authored English text scores **1** —
  a weak signal by design, and empty in a non-English short, so a panel has to
  be earned by `visualTerms` alone there
- `+0.5` for no baked-in text, `+0.25` for a band at or above 26%

Below a score of 3 there is no match and Grok is asked instead. A panel that
does not fit is worse than no panel: a wrong picture actively misteaches.
Scoring is deterministic and ties break on panel id, so the same teaching
always resolves to the same panel — which the render contract requires, and
which also means re-running a short returns the picture the creator approved.

## Layout metrics

Two numbers per panel, measured from the pixels rather than guessed
(`scripts/measure-doodle-bands.py`):

- **Band** — how far down the panel the paper stays clean across the centre
  column, where the sentence sits. The template lays a scrim of the panel's own
  paper colour over `max(band, 26%)`, so on a panel that already
  reserves a clean upper quarter the scrim is invisible, and on a full-bleed
  one it manufactures the band. Rows marked `*` are full-bleed and rely on
  the manufactured band.
- **Paper** — the page stock, sampled from the panel's top edge, so that scrim
  seam cannot be seen.

18 of 61 panels have a natural band of 26% or more.

## Baked-in text

30 panels have English words drawn into the art — banners, speech
bubbles, handwritten captions. They stay eligible, because the set is small and
each panel earns its place, but the matcher breaks ties against them: English
lettering under a Hindi sentence reads as a mistake. Prefer a text-free panel
when both fit.
